issues.t: Engine burns oil
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, sometimes a quart every few hundred miles, often with no visible leak or smoke. Some owners see soot on the rear bumper, oily spark plugs, or a ticking noise when the oil runs low.
issues.why: The 1.8L engine shared with the Toyota Corolla is known for oil consumption, usually starting between about 45,000 and 90,000 miles. Owners and mechanics most often blame piston oil rings that stick with carbon and stop scraping oil off the cylinder walls. It is by far the most reported Prizm problem, worst on the 2001 model.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up and top up as needed; running it low can ruin the engine. Some owners slow consumption with regular synthetic oil changes and a piston-ring cleaning treatment, but the lasting fix is new piston rings or a replacement engine.

issues.t: Airbags failed to deploy in a crash
issues.sym: Owners report front airbags that did not go off in frontal crashes, sometimes with injuries. Some also report the airbag warning light staying on even after repairs.
issues.why: Airbags are the top complaint area for the 1996-2000 Prizm in federal complaint data. The reports don't point to one confirmed cause, and some describe failed airbag sensors.
issues.next: If the airbag light is on, have the system scanned; the airbags may not work until it is fixed. Check your VIN for open recalls.

issues.t: Airbag can go off unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: The airbags may deploy without a real crash, for example after a hard jolt from the road.
issues.why: GM recalled certain 1997 Prizms (NHTSA 97V043) because the airbag system could deploy unexpectedly and injure occupants.
issues.next: Have a Chevrolet dealer check whether the recall was done on your car.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold
issues.sym: The air conditioning blows warm or only slightly cool air, or the compressor won't engage.
issues.why: A/C compressor failures and refrigerant leaks from lines, seals and the receiver-drier are among the most common repairs reported by Prizm owners.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested before paying for a recharge, since a leak will just empty it again. A failed compressor needs replacing along with the receiver-drier.

issues.t: Heater fan works only on some speeds
issues.sym: The blower works on high but not on the lower settings, or stops working on some speeds.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor, which sets the fan speeds, is one of the most reported Prizm repairs.
issues.next: A blower resistor is a small part, usually behind the glove box.

issues.t: Inside door handle breaks
issues.sym: The inside door handle snaps or goes loose and won't open the door.
issues.why: The interior door handle is the single most reported repair in TrueDelta's Prizm survey; the plastic handle cracks with age.
issues.next: Replacement handles can be installed at home or by a shop. Until then, open the door from the outside.

issues.t: Wheel bearing hum or grinding
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed and may change when you turn.
issues.why: Worn front or rear wheel bearings and hub assemblies are a common Prizm repair.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked; a badly worn bearing can overheat and fail.

issues.t: Worn tie rod ends cause shake or loose steering
issues.sym: The steering wheel shakes, feels loose, or the car wanders, often with uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Worn tie rod ends are a common Prizm repair, and steering wheel shake and tie rod complaints are reported on the Geo version too.
issues.next: Have the front end checked and aligned. Worn tie rods should be replaced promptly because a failed one can cause loss of steering control.

issues.t: Clunk from the stabilizer bar links
issues.sym: A clunk or rattle from the front over bumps.
issues.why: The stabilizer bar end links and bushings wear out and are a commonly reported repair.
issues.next: Replacing the links and bushings is usually quick.

issues.t: Exhaust manifold gasket leak
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing noise from the engine area, louder on a cold start, and sometimes an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The exhaust manifold gasket can fail and leak, as reported by Prizm owners.
issues.next: Have it fixed soon; exhaust leaks near the engine can let fumes into the cabin.

issues.t: Clutch slipping or worn
issues.sym: On manual cars, engine revs rise without the car speeding up, especially in higher gears, or the clutch engages very high.
issues.why: Clutch wear is among the repairs reported by Prizm owners.
issues.next: Have the clutch checked; once it slips it will only get worse.

issues.t: ABS warning light on
issues.sym: The ABS light stays on, with trouble codes 46 and 86 stored.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for the ABS light coming on with these codes on the Geo Prizm.
issues.next: Normal brakes still work, but anti-lock may be off. Have the ABS codes read and the bulletin checked.

issues.t: Steering column squeaks when turning in hot weather
issues.sym: A squeak from the steering column when you turn the wheel, mostly when the car is hot inside.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for this noise; the fix is lubricating the lower steering column bushing.
issues.next: A shop can lubricate the bushing quickly. It is a noise only.

issues.t: Seat belts don't retract or latch properly
issues.sym: A front seat belt that won't retract, locks up, or won't latch reliably.
issues.why: Seat belt complaints, especially for the front retractors, make up a large share of complaints for the Geo Prizm.
issues.next: Seat belts are critical safety parts. Have a faulty belt replaced rather than repaired.

issues.t: Automatic transmission failure
issues.sym: Slipping, no engagement, or the car won't move in gear.
issues.why: Transmission failure is the top reported problem on the 1997 Geo Prizm, usually at high mileage.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition first. A used or rebuilt transmission is often the practical fix on an older car.

issues.t: Misfire with check engine light on
issues.sym: Rough running or shaking, loss of power, and a check engine light.
issues.why: Misfire with the engine light on is the top reported problem on the 1996 Geo Prizm, usually at high mileage, and typically fixed with ignition parts.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Plugs, wires or the distributor cap and rotor are the usual suspects on this engine.

issues.t: Seat belt warning light flashes or stays on
issues.sym: The seat belt reminder light flashes or comes on whether or not you are buckled.
issues.why: Owners report a faulty buckle switch, and dealers quoted replacing the whole seat belt assembly.
issues.next: Ask a shop whether just the buckle can be replaced instead of the full belt.

issues.t: Hood can pop open while driving
issues.sym: The hood flies up while driving, blocking the view and sometimes cracking the windshield.
issues.why: Owners report the hood latch not holding the hood closed at speed.
issues.next: Make sure the hood is fully latched and have the latch and safety catch cleaned, lubricated or replaced if it doesn't hold firmly.

issues.t: ABS kicks in at the wrong time
issues.sym: The anti-lock brakes pulse or engage unexpectedly in normal stops, making stopping distances longer.
issues.why: Owners report ABS engaging unexpectedly; a dirty or failing wheel speed sensor is a common cause of this.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read and the wheel speed sensors and tone rings inspected.

issues.t: Hesitation or stalling with check engine light
issues.sym: The engine hesitates when accelerating, worst on cold starts, or stalls when coming to a stop, and the check engine light may stay on.
issues.why: Owners report hesitation and stalling along with a lean-mixture code; the cause was often not found.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the system checked for vacuum leaks and a dirty airflow sensor, which commonly cause lean codes.
